newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds up with foreign markets, eyes on EMU.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds up with foreign markets, eyes on EMU.

text.p: Danish bond prices rose on Wednesday, following foreign bourses up in a market with positive undertone but focused on EMU developments.
"We have followed foreign markets up today so far in fairly busy trade with a close eye on the various EMU developments and outside trends and will continue to do so," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.34 point from Tuesday's close at 111.58, yielding 6.24 percent in turnover of 1.5 billion crowns while the forthcoming seven percent 2007 benchmark was up 0.18 point at 104.20, with the yield at 6.43 percent in two billion crown turnover.
THe 2006's June future rose 0.32 point to 111.54 with four contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.25 point to 89.85.
The crown traded at 3.8071 per mark at 1145 gmt, up a smidgen from around 3.8075 at the opening.
The 2006 benchmark's 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed one basis point to 49 from Tuesday, with the 2007-bund differential at an unchanged 68.
The Central Bank was active on the market selling seven percent 2024 bonds as part of its routine financing operations.
